technical.lead: FMRB EO T-3: FCC chief joins witness slate, Brennan + Stanford amicus
technical.body: The Frontier Model Review Board executive-order interagency-review push enters the three-business-day window before the May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing. House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology Chair sends a Tuesday-morning joint letter to White House OSTP with Senator Mark Warner requesting any signed executive order include a parallel 30-day House Energy and Commerce technical review window mirroring the Senate cyber-subcommittee classified-briefing protocol. Senator Warner's office confirms a sixth witness, the Federal Communications Commission Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Chief, joining the previously-confirmed NIST Director Locascio, ODNI cyber lead, NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative, and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director. The Brennan Center for Justice and the Center for Internet and Society at Stanford file a joint Tuesday amicus letter joining the existing twelve-organization coalition, narrowing the focus to the State Farm reasoned-decision-record requirement plus a paired sixty-day Defense Production Act Section 708 public-comment window aligned to the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window. OSTP holds its line that the draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22.

technical.lead: Indo-Pacific reciprocity hits 11 jurisdictions; Chile + Mexico join
technical.body: The Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter reaches its first eleven-jurisdiction Tuesday count and adds the first formal Latin American observer. Thailand's National Cyber Security Agency plus the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society jointly publish a Tuesday entry note signaling intent to enter the Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI memorandum-of-cooperation cohort as a formal observer with a 180-day domestic-consultation window targeting Q1 2027 mirror signature. The cohort now spans eleven named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand as observers) plus the originating UK and EU. Chile's National Cybersecurity Coordination Office separately confirms exploratory observer status, citing its February 2026 national AI strategy and the OECD GENAI working group seat as the procedural baseline; the Mexican Federal Institute of Telecommunications signals it will join Chile under a parallel exploratory track. Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind reaffirm cohort participation; the operational threshold remains Mythos-class capability plus GPT-5.5-class capability. The United States recognition gap is now a full Tuesday wider than the Monday baseline with the first cross-hemispheric extension confirmed.

technical.lead: Pydantic AI CVE-2026-44892 extends agent-loader taxonomy to eight CVEs
technical.body: A fresh agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops Tuesday-morning Pacific time, this time on the inference-routing tier rather than the agent-checkpoint loader path. Pydantic AI CVE-2026-44892 (CVSS 8.4) is an authenticated server-side request forgery in the tool-result-cache validator that lets an attacker pivot from a connected message broker to internal cloud-metadata endpoints, mirroring the Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 manifest-fetcher exposure pattern but at the inference-routing tier; the Pydantic maintainer team ships v0.4.7 same-day with the patch plus a paired backport advisory for the v0.3.x and v0.2.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Tuesday extended addendum updating its Monday taxonomy from seven to eight agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs (adding Pydantic AI to CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangChain plus LangGraph and LiteLLM). DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Tuesday joint follow-up preprint (arxiv 2605.06712) extending the Monday signed-checkpoint paper with a runtime-verifier integration pattern covering the inference-routing tier; Microsoft, LangChain, CrewAI, and Pydantic AI publish parallel Tuesday commitments to ship as default in the next minor release alongside the load-time signed-checkpoint primitive.

technical.lead: Cerebras tags $197 high; SEC opens Tenstorrent 30-60 day review
technical.body: Cerebras CBRS Tuesday session prints a clean intraday extension after Monday's gap-up. The opening print at $193.20 lifts the stock 2.0 percent from Monday's $189.40 close, with the high-of-day touching $197.10 at 13:45 EDT before settling into a $194-$196 range; trailing-five-session turnover crosses $4.8B with the institutional-buyside cumulative net position estimated at 31 percent of float. Morgan Stanley adds a Tuesday-afternoon best-ideas-list inclusion at the $192 target; Bernstein holds its $172 Market-Perform floor pending Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close timeline visibility. CBRS options trade with a 4.1x call-skew at 14:00 EDT (approximately 61,400 calls versus 14,950 puts) — the widest call-skew since the IPO debut session. The SEC Division of Corporation Finance issues Tenstorrent a Tuesday confidential-submission acknowledgement under the JOBS Act EGC framework, formally opening the 30-60 day review window with an early-August public-filing target intact per Jim Keller's Monday investor-relations note; the Corp Fin sample comment letter precedent on AI-services-revenue measurement basis from May 8 plus the single-counterparty risk-factor exhibit pattern anchored by the Cerebras CBRS S-1 are flagged in the working notes as the operative precedent set. SambaNova adds Barclays Capital as fifth joint lead bookrunner with the late-June confidential-submission target unchanged.

technical.lead: Unsloth adds dual-Hopper backward pass + first signed-checkpoint primitive
technical.body: Unsloth ships its Tuesday changelog adding a fifth refinement track to the multi-GPU NCCL backend for the router-only LoRA recipe, plus a research-first integration with the Tuesday signed-checkpoint adoption wave. The update brings a kernel-fused tensor-parallel router-attention backward pass on dual-Hopper workstation tiers (H100 SXM5 plus H100 PCIe combinations) reporting a further 14 percent training-step time reduction versus the Monday tensor-parallel forward-pass-only mode plus a 9 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on Llama 4 Behemoth router-only training, a deterministic signature-verified checkpoint save and load path tied to the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic Monday joint preprint Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature chain (Unsloth becomes the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target), an extended ONNX export path supporting FP8 quantization for the router-only adapters targeting the Nvidia Blackwell deployment cohort, plus a community-contributed recipe for the Anthropic Claude 3.7 Haiku Mixture-of-Experts open-weights release showing 7 percent peak combined VRAM on a dual-RTX 6000 Ada workstation. A third Hacker News reproduction lands within hours documenting the Mac Studio M4 Ultra workstation completing the Mixtral 8x22B router-only recipe through the new signed-checkpoint primitive at 13 percent peak combined VRAM, extending commodity-and-prosumer-hardware accessibility to the Apple Silicon tier.
